content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
American Honda Motor Co. Inc. has recalled approximately 12,600 off-road motorcycles from the 2025 and 2026 model years, including the CRF250R, CRF250RX, CRF250RWE, CRF450R, CRF450RX, and CRF450RWE models. These motorcycles were sold across the United States through authorized Honda Powersports dealers between June 2024 and March 2026, with prices ranging from $8,900 to $13,200. Additionally, about six units were sold in Canada.

The recall addresses a defect in the handlebar clamp that may cause the handlebar to rotate unexpectedly during operation. This defect creates a significant crash hazard that could result in serious injury or death. So far, the company has received one report of a crash linked to this issue, but no injuries have been reported.

Owners of the affected motorcycles are urged to stop riding immediately and schedule a free inspection and repair with an authorized Honda Powersports dealer to replace or repair the handlebar clamp as needed.

content.text: To determine if your motorcycle is part of this recall, check the model year and model designation. You can also locate the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) on your motorcycle, typically found near the steering head or frame, and verify it with your dealer or the recall notice to confirm if your unit is included.

content.subtitle: What Consumers Should Do
content.text: If you own one of the recalled motorcycles, stop riding it immediately to avoid the risk of a crash. Contact an authorized Honda Powersports dealer to schedule a free inspection of the handlebar clamp. If the clamp is found to be defective, the dealer will repair or replace it at no cost to you. For more information or assistance, call American Honda Motor toll-free at 866-784-1870, Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. PT, or visit Honda Powersports Recalls.

content.subtitle: Risk Overview
content.text: The handlebar clamp on these recalled motorcycles can fail to hold the handlebar securely, allowing it to rotate unexpectedly while riding. This sudden movement can cause the rider to lose control, increasing the risk of a crash. Such crashes can lead to serious injuries or even fatalities. The risk is serious enough that Honda advises owners to stop using the motorcycles until the clamp is inspected and repaired.

description: Build-A-Bear recalls Heartwarming Hugs Bears sold early 2026 due to detachable zipper slider choking hazard; refunds available at stores or online.
subtitle: The Heartwarming Hugs Bear sold January–March 2026 has a side pouch zipper slider that can detach, creating a choking hazard; consumers should stop use and seek refund from Build-A-Bear Workshop.

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: The Heartwarming Hugs Bear sold by Build-A-Bear Workshop from January through March 2026 has a side pouch zipper slider that can detach, posing a choking hazard to children. Consumers should immediately stop using the bear and return it to Build-A-Bear for a refund or gift card.

content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
Build-A-Bear Workshop is recalling approximately 36,000 Heartwarming Hugs Bears sold in the United States and an additional 520 sold in Canada. These bears were available from January through March 2026 at Build-A-Bear Workshop stores and online for about $48 each.

The product features a side pouch with a zipper slider that can detach during use. This detaching zipper slider creates a serious choking hazard for children. While no injuries have been reported in the United States, one incident was reported in the United Kingdom where the zipper slider detached while the bear was being used.

Consumers who have purchased the Heartwarming Hugs Bear are urged to stop using it immediately and follow the recall instructions provided by Build-A-Bear Workshop to obtain a refund or replacement.

If a consumer is unable to return their Heartwarming Hugs Bear to a local store, they can visit www.buildabear.com/recalls for more information or call Build-A-Bear to receive a free return shipping label to return the recalled bear and to receive a refund check in the form of original payment or in the form of a digital gift card to use on the firm's website.

content.subtitle: How to Identify the Recalled Product
content.text:
Consumers should look for the Heartwarming Hugs Bear featuring a side pouch with a zipper slider. The zipper is located on the side of the bear’s pouch and is the part that can detach. The bears were sold by Build-A-Bear Workshop and may have been purchased in-store or online during the specified timeframe.

Images of the recalled bear show a plush bear with a heart-shaped bead bag inside the pouch and a zipper slider on the side pouch. If your bear matches this description and was purchased between January and March 2026, it is part of the recall.

content.subtitle: What Consumers Should Do
content.text:
Stop using the Heartwarming Hugs Bear immediately. Consumers should return the bear to any local Build-A-Bear Workshop store to receive a refund. The refund can be issued as the original payment or as a gift card redeemable toward any Make-Your-Own furry friend or other merchandise available at Build-A-Bear.

If returning to a store is not possible, visit www.buildabear.com/recalls for instructions. Consumers can also call Build-A-Bear at 844-541-0144 to request a free return shipping label. Upon return, a refund check or digital gift card will be issued.

content.subtitle: Risk Overview
content.text: The zipper slider on the side pouch of the Heartwarming Hugs Bear can come off during normal play. If a child puts the detached zipper slider in their mouth, it could block their airway and cause choking. This hazard is serious because choking can lead to injury or death if not promptly addressed. The recall aims to prevent such risks by removing the affected bears from use.

content.subtitle: Who May Be Affected
content.text: This recall affects anyone who purchased a Heartwarming Hugs Bear from Build-A-Bear Workshop stores or online between January and March 2026. Approximately 36,000 units were sold in the U.S. and 520 in Canada. The bears were sold for about $48 each.

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: CBC Group is recalling about 227,500 Stephan Baby Boo Bunnie and Friends children's toys because the included plastic cubes can break into small, sharp pieces that pose choking and laceration hazards. Consumers should stop using the toys immediately and contact CBC Group for a refund or store credit.

content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
CBC Group has recalled approximately 227,500 units of Stephan Baby Boo Bunnie and Friends children's toys, including about 1,400 sold in Canada. These toys were available from August 2017 through January 2026 at independent stores nationwide and online retailers such as Stephanbaby.com, Amazon.com, Walmart.com, and Target.com, with prices ranging from $2 to $9.

The recall focuses on the plastic cubes included with the toys, which can crack or break into small parts or sharp edges. This defect creates a risk of choking and laceration injuries to children. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) has received 20 reports of the cubes breaking, including one incident where a child swallowed sharp pieces.

Consumers are advised to stop using the recalled toys immediately and follow CBC Group’s instructions to obtain a refund or store credit to prevent injury.

The cube also has a sewn-in label with this branding. The recalled toys were sold for prices between $2 and $9. If you have a toy with these characteristics purchased within the stated timeframe, it may be part of the recall.

content.subtitle: What Consumers Should Do
content.text:
Stop using the recalled toys immediately and remove the plastic cube from children’s reach. Contact CBC Group to request a refund or store credit. If you have proof of purchase, you will receive a full refund. Without proof of purchase, you can receive a $10 refund by check or a $20 store credit for stephanbaby.com.

Consumers are asked to write "Recalled" in permanent marker on the indented area of the cube and upload a photo of the toy and marked cube at https://recall.stephanbaby.com/. After this, you will receive a prepaid shipping label to return the cube.

For assistance, contact CBC Group toll-free at 877-725-5591 from 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. PT or email boobunnie@stephanbaby.com.

content.subtitle: Risk Overview
content.text: The hazard arises because the plastic cubes attached to the Stephan Baby Boo Bunnie and Friends toys can break apart, producing small fragments or sharp edges. These broken pieces can be easily swallowed or cause cuts, posing a serious choking and laceration risk to young children who often put toys in their mouths. The risk is significant enough that the CPSC has documented multiple reports of breakage and at least one ingestion incident.

The recall stems from the packaging not being child-resistant and missing mandatory labeling statements required by the Poison Prevention Packaging Act. The nasal spray contains an imidazoline ingredient that can cause serious injury or illness if ingested by young children. To date, no injuries have been reported.

Consumers who have these nasal spray bottles should follow Bayer’s instructions to obtain a refund and safely dispose of the recalled products.

Bayer HealthCare LLC is voluntarily recalling about 786,100 travel size Afrin® Original Nasal Spray 6 mL bottles. These nasal sprays were primarily sold at convenience stores and travel locations such as airports between September 2024 and April 2026, with prices ranging from $7 to $9.

The recall stems from the packaging not being child-resistant and missing mandatory labeling statements required by the Poison Prevention Packaging Act. The nasal spray contains an imidazoline ingredient that can cause serious injury or illness if ingested by young children. To date, no injuries have been reported.

Consumers who have these nasal spray bottles should follow Bayer’s instructions to obtain a refund and safely dispose of the recalled products.

description: Qumeney bicycle light sets sold on Amazon are recalled for accessible button cell batteries posing ingestion risks; consumers should stop use and contact Smfanlus for.
subtitle: About 2,800 Qumeney bicycle light sets sold on Amazon from March 2024 to February 2026 contain accessible button cell batteries posing ingestion hazards; consumers should stop use and seek refunds from Smfanlus.
keywords: The recalled bicycle lights violate the mandatory standard for consumer products with button cell and coin batteries because they contain button cell batteries that can be accessed easily by children, posing an ingestion hazard. Additionally, the bicycle lights do not have the warnings required under Reese's Law. When button cell or coin batteries are swallowed, the ingested batteries can cause serious injuries, internal chemical burns, and death.

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: The Qumeney Bicycle Light Sets sold in 6-pack and 24-pack options on Amazon are recalled because their button cell batteries can be easily accessed by children, creating a serious ingestion hazard. Consumers should stop using these lights immediately and contact Smfanlus for a full refund.

content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
The recall involves approximately 2,800 Qumeney Bicycle Light Sets distributed by Xiamen Fanlu Technology Co., Ltd., operating as Smfanlus, based in China. These lights were sold online at Amazon.com from March 2024 through February 2026 in 6-pack and 24-pack configurations, priced between $7 and $18.

The bicycle lights contain button cell batteries that children can easily access, violating mandatory safety standards for consumer products with such batteries. Additionally, the products lack the required warnings mandated by Reese's Law. To date, no injuries have been reported related to this hazard.

Consumers who purchased these bicycle light sets are urged to stop using them immediately and follow the recall instructions to obtain a refund.

When button cell or coin batteries are swallowed, the ingested batteries can cause serious injuries, internal chemical burns, and death.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled bicycle lights immediately and contact Smfanlus for a full refund. content.subtitle: What Consumers Should Do

You will be asked to send a photo showing the destroyed parts of the light components after battery removal. Additional information and refund instructions are available by visiting the seller’s Amazon page and clicking the "Recall" link at the top.

The recalled products also do not include the safety warnings required by law, which help alert consumers to this danger.

description: Acer recalls AES015 folding electric scooters sold 2023-2026 due to a loose screw causing fall hazards; consumers should stop use and get free repairs from Acer.
subtitle: About 510 Acer AES015 two-wheeled folding electric scooters sold in the U.S. from June 2023 to February 2026 have a loose screw hazard causing sudden folding; free repair tools available from Acer.

A loose screw can cause the front tube to fold down unexpectedly, posing a risk of injury from a fall hazard.

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: Acer is recalling about 510 AES015 folding electric scooters sold in the U.S. because a loose screw can cause the front tube to fold unexpectedly, posing a fall risk. Consumers should stop using these scooters immediately and contact Acer for free repair tools and instructions to fix the issue.

content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
The recall covers approximately 510 Acer AES015 two-wheeled folding electric scooters sold in the United States between June 2023 and February 2026. Additional units were sold in Canada (about 311) and Mexico (about 150). These scooters were available online at Acer.com, Amazon.com, and in BrandMart stores, with prices ranging from $70 to $245.

The defect involves a loose screw that can cause the scooter's front tube to fold down unexpectedly during use. This sudden folding creates a fall hazard for riders. While Acer has not received any injury reports in the U.S., one international incident resulted in minor abrasions from a fall.

Consumers are urged to stop using the recalled scooters immediately and contact Acer to receive free repair tools and guidance on tightening the screw to eliminate the hazard.

Contact Acer America Corporation to request free repair tools and instructions on how to tighten the loose screw to prevent the front tube from folding unexpectedly. This unexpected folding can cause the rider to lose balance and fall, increasing the risk of injury. Although no injuries have been reported in the U.S., the potential for falls makes this a serious safety concern.

title: Acer Recalls AES015 Folding Electric Scooters Due to Fall Hazard
Title: Acer Recalls AES015 Folding Electric Scooters Due to Fall Hazard
Description:
The recall covers approximately 510 Acer AES015 two-wheeled folding electric scooters sold in the United States between June 2023 and February 2026. Additional units were sold in Canada (about 311) and Mexico (about 150). These scooters were available online at Acer.com, Amazon.com, and in BrandMart stores, with prices ranging from $70 to $245.

The defect involves a loose screw that can cause the scooter's front tube to fold down unexpectedly during use. This sudden folding creates a fall hazard for riders. While Acer has not received any injury reports in the U.S., one international incident resulted in minor abrasions from a fall.

Consumers are urged to stop using the recalled scooters immediately and contact Acer to receive free repair tools and guidance on tightening the screw to eliminate the hazard.

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: Earthtec 7 3/8-inch pool drain covers sold online at Amazon.com between October 2025 and April 2026 have been recalled due to entrapment and drowning hazards. content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
The recall involves approximately 211 Earthtec 7 3/8-inch pool drain covers sold online at Amazon.com from October 2025 through April 2026 for about $15 each. These drain covers were manufactured in China by Shenzhen Qiangonghui Technology Co., Ltd., operating as Tonyidea.

These products fail to meet the entrapment protection requirements of the Virginia Graeme Baker Pool and Spa Safety Act (VGBA). This noncompliance creates a serious hazard where swimmers and bathers can become trapped by the suction of the pool drain, posing a risk of drowning.

No injuries have been reported in connection with this recall. Pool owners and operators who purchased these drain covers are urged to take immediate action to prevent potential harm.

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: Residential Elevators is recalling approximately 450 StrikeLock hoistway door locking devices installed in residential elevators nationwide. content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
Residential Elevators has issued a recall for about 450 StrikeLock hoistway door locking devices installed in residential elevator systems across the United States. content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: Thermos has recalled about 8.2 million Stainless King Food Jars and Sportsman Food & Beverage Bottles sold between March 2008 and July 2024 because their stoppers can forcefully eject when opened, posing serious injury risks. Consumers should stop using these products immediately and contact Thermos for a free replacement stopper or bottle.

content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
Thermos is recalling approximately 8.2 million Stainless King Food Jars and Sportsman Food & Beverage Bottles sold across the United States and online from around March 2008 through July 2024. The affected products include the Stainless King 3000 and 3020 Food Jars and the Sportsman 3010 Food & Beverage Bottles. These items were retailed at major stores such as Target, Walmart, and Amazon for about $30 each.

The recall was prompted by reports that the stopper in these containers can eject forcefully when opened if perishable food or beverages have been stored for a long time. This can cause serious impact injuries and lacerations. Thermos has received 27 injury reports, including three cases of permanent vision loss after consumers were struck in the eye.

Consumers are advised to stop using the recalled products immediately and contact Thermos to obtain a free replacement stopper or bottle. The recall is managed by Thermos L.L.C. of Schaumburg, Illinois, with the products manufactured in China and Malaysia.

  • Stainless King 3020 Food Jar
  • Sportsman 3010 Food & Beverage Bottle

These products typically sold for about $30 and were manufactured in China or Malaysia. The stopper on the recalled items does not have a pressure relief feature in the center, which can be visually confirmed. content.subtitle: What Consumers Should Do
content.text:
Stop using the recalled Thermos Food Jars and Bottles immediately to avoid injury. For the Stainless King 3000 and 3020 Food Jars, consumers should discard the stopper and send a photo of the disposed stopper to Thermos to receive a free replacement pressure relief stopper.

For the Sportsman 3010 Bottles, consumers must return the recalled bottle to Thermos using a prepaid shipping label provided by the company. Contact Thermos online at https://support.thermos.com or visit https://www.thermos.com and click "Contact Us" or "Recall Info." You can also call 662-563-6822 from 7 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. CT Monday through Friday for assistance.

Opening the container can cause the stopper to eject suddenly and forcefully, which may result in impact injuries or cuts. This risk is serious enough that some consumers have experienced permanent vision loss.

editorialBrief.metaDescription: BlissfulDestiny recalls Magnetic Stick Figure Sets sold at Walmart.com for loose magnets posing ingestion hazards; consumers should stop use and seek refunds.
editorialBrief.quickAnswerHtml: BlissfulDestiny has recalled about 140 Magnetic Stick Figure Sets sold online at Walmart.com between May and October 2025 because they contain loose magnets that can be swallowed by children, creating serious internal injuries. Consumers should immediately stop using these toys and contact BlissfulDestiny via email to receive a full refund.
editorialBrief.recallSummaryHtml:
The recalled product is the BlissfulDestiny Magnetic Stick Figure Sets, sold for approximately $13 each online at Walmart.com from May 2025 through October 2025. About 140 units were sold during this period. These toys contain loose, high-powered magnets that violate mandatory toy safety standards.

The hazard stems from the magnets potentially being swallowed by children. If ingested, the magnets can attract each other or other metal objects inside the digestive tract, which may cause severe injuries such as intestinal perforations, twisting, blockages, blood poisoning, or even death. To date, no injuries have been reported in connection with this recall.

Consumers who purchased these sets should stop using them immediately and follow the recall instructions to obtain a refund by contacting BlissfulDestiny.
editorialBrief.riskOverviewHtml: The main risk involves children swallowing the loose magnets included in the stick figure sets. Once inside the body, these magnets can pull together or attach to metal objects, causing serious internal damage. This can lead to complications like holes or blockages in the intestines and potentially life-threatening infections. Because of these dangers, the product does not meet required safety standards for toys.
editorialBrief.whoIsAffectedHtml: This recall affects anyone who bought the BlissfulDestiny Magnetic Stick Figure Sets online at Walmart.com between May and October 2025. The product was marketed as a toy and sold for about $13 each. Families with young children should be especially cautious, as children are at risk of swallowing the magnets.
editorialBrief.howToIdentifyProductHtml: Consumers should check for the BlissfulDestiny Magnetic Stick Figure Sets purchased online from Walmart.com during the specified timeframe. The product is a set of magnetic stick figures sold for about $13. Visual identification can be aided by the product images showing the magnetic stick figures. If you have this toy and it matches the description and purchase period, it is subject to the recall.
editorialBrief.whatToDoHtml: Stop using the magnetic stick figure sets immediately and keep them away from children. Consumers should dispose of the recalled product by throwing it away and then email a photo of the discarded toy to BlissfulDestiny at Blissful_Destiny@outlook.com. This will initiate the refund process. Do not attempt to repair or continue using the toy.

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: 32 Degrees has recalled about 207,806 pairs of heated socks sold at Costco and Costco.com from August 2025 to March 2026 because wearing them during high-intensity activities can cause burns. Consumers should stop using the socks immediately and return them to Costco for a full refund.

content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
The recall involves 32 Degrees Heated Socks equipped with rechargeable battery packs designed to provide warmth. These socks were sold at Costco stores and online at Costco.com between August 2025 and March 2026, with prices ranging from $30 to $46. Approximately 207,806 units are affected by this recall.

The socks pose a burn hazard when worn during high-intensity activities that generate a combination of heat, friction, moisture, and pressure. This combination can lead to burns, as evidenced by 14 reported heat-related incidents, 13 of which involved first- or second-degree burns. The socks were imported from China by David Peyser Sportswear doing business as 32 Degrees, based in New York.

Consumers who purchased these heated socks should immediately stop using them and return the product to Costco for a full refund. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) and 32 Degrees are collaborating to protect consumers through this recall.

remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using the heated socks and return them to Costco for a full refund.

content.subtitle: How to Identify the Recalled Product
content.text: Consumers should check their socks for the 32 Degrees brand label and confirm purchase from Costco stores or Costco.com within the specified timeframe (August 2025 to March 2026). The recalled socks include a rechargeable battery pack designed to provide warmth. Packaging and user manuals may also accompany the product. If your socks match these details, they are part of the recall.

content.subtitle: What Consumers Should Do
content.text: If you have purchased the recalled 32 Degrees Heated Socks, stop using them immediately to avoid the risk of burns. Return the socks to any Costco store for a full refund. For additional information or assistance, contact 32 Degrees toll-free at 833-997-2452 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET, Monday through Friday, email recall@32degrees.com, or visit 32degrees.com/recall and click on "Sock Recall" under the "Support" section.

content.subtitle: Risk Overview
content.text: The burn hazard arises because the socks’ rechargeable battery packs generate heat to keep feet warm. When combined with intense physical activity, which produces additional heat, friction, moisture, and pressure, the socks can overheat and cause skin burns. This risk is particularly relevant during activities that increase body heat and movement, creating conditions that the socks were not designed to safely handle.

content.subtitle: Who May Be Affected
content.text: This recall affects anyone who purchased 32 Degrees Heated Socks from Costco stores or online at Costco.com between August 2025 and March 2026. The socks were sold for prices between $30 and $46. If you own these socks, especially if you use them for high-intensity activities, you should consider this recall important for your safety.
